level.title: Arabic A2+ — Holding a chat
goals: React, follow up and keep a conversation alive
Tell a short story in order, with a scene and an ending
Invite, accept, decline — on the phone and in person

lessons.title: Reactions that mean something
lessons.learn: Arabic conversation is fed by reactions: حقاً؟ (really?), طبعاً (of course), مستحيل (no way), عجيب (strange). They buy time and, more importantly, they hand the floor back.

grammar.title: React, then ask
grammar.explain: حقاً؟ وماذا حدث بعد ذلك؟ A reaction alone can end a turn; adding و + a question gives the floor back. طبعاً agrees, مستحيل refuses to believe — check which one the moment needs.

examples.en: Really? I did not know that.
Of course, that is clear.
No way! How much was the price?

mistakes.why: As a reaction, حقاً stands alone and takes a question mark.
Contradicting yourself inside one reaction kills the signal.

dialogue.en: I finally bought the house.

dialogue.t: حقاً؟ مبروك! وماذا حدث مع البنك؟
dialogue.r: ḥaqqan? mabrūk! wa-mādhā ḥadatha maʿa al-bank?
dialogue.en: Really? Congratulations! And what happened with the bank?
They finally agreed after two months.

dialogue.t: مستحيل! شهران كاملان! الحمد لله على كل حال.
dialogue.r: mustaḥīl! shahrān kāmilān! al-ḥamdu li-llāh ʿalā kull ḥāl.
dialogue.en: No way! Two whole months! Thank God for everything.

lessons.title: Following up: وبعد ذلك؟
lessons.learn: A conversation dies when nobody asks the next question. وماذا حدث؟، ماذا بعد؟، ولماذا؟ keep the partner talking, and كيف كان ذلك؟ asks for the feeling, not the fact.

grammar.title: Follow-up ladder
grammar.pattern: mādhā ḥadatha? → wa-baʿda dhālika? → wa-kayfa kāna?
grammar.explain: Each question aims a step deeper: the event, the next event, then the evaluation. أخبرني أكثر is the shortest way to say 'I am listening'.

examples.en: And what happened after the interview?
How did you feel?
Tell me more — this matters.

mistakes.why: The verb حدث takes لـ for the person affected.
Three follow-ups in a row turn interest into an interrogation.

dialogue.en: I arrived late at the airport yesterday.
And what happened after that?
They cancelled the flight, so I slept in the hotel.
How did you feel?

lessons.title: Showing interest: ما شاء الله، يا للعجب
lessons.learn: Praise and wonder carry conversations: ما شاء الله، كم هذا جميل، يا للعجب، الله يعطيك العافية. They are formulaic by design — the formula is the politeness.

grammar.title: Exclamations
grammar.pattern: mā shāʾa Allāh · kam hādhā + adjective · yā li-l- + noun
grammar.explain: ما شاء الله، عمل ممتاز! كم هذا جميل! يا للعجب، ما توقّعت ذلك. The formula does the social work; the words after it make it specific.

examples.t: ما شاء الله، بيتك جميل جداً.
examples.r: mā shāʾa Allāh, baytuk jamīl jiddan.
examples.en: What God wills — your house is very beautiful.
How delicious this food is!

examples.t: الله يعطيك العافية، تعبتَ من أجلي.
examples.r: Allāh yuʿṭīk al-ʿāfiya, taʿibta min ajlī.
examples.en: May God give you health — you tired yourself for me.

mistakes.wrong: ما شاء الله، لكن البيت قديم.
mistakes.why: ما شاء الله is praise; balancing it with a criticism in the same breath breaks the formula.
كم + demonstrative + adjective is the fixed order.

dialogue.en: This is my son — he passed the exam.

dialogue.t: ما شاء الله! كم هذا خبر جميل!
dialogue.r: mā shāʾa Allāh! kam hādhā khabar jamīl!
dialogue.en: What God wills! What lovely news!
Thank you — he worked hard this year.
May God give him health and always grant him success.

lessons.title: In order: أولاً، ثمّ، بعد ذلك، أخيراً
lessons.learn: Four connectors turn four sentences into a story: أولاً، ثمّ، بعد ذلك، أخيراً. Arabic also uses فـ for the immediate next step and ثمّ for the deliberate one.

grammar.title: Story order
grammar.explain: أولاً وصلنا إلى المطار. ثمّ انتظرنا ساعتين. وبعد ذلك أقلعت الطائرة. وأخيراً وصلنا في الليل. One connector per step, one step per sentence.

examples.en: At first I did not know anyone.
Then I met Sara.
And finally we became friends.

mistakes.wrong: أولاً ثمّ بعد ذلك أخيراً حدث كل شيء.
mistakes.why: All four connectors in one sentence is a list, not a story.

mistakes.wrong: ثمّ وصلتُ، وبعد ذلك وصلتُ أيضاً.
mistakes.why: Repeating the same event under two connectors stalls the story.

dialogue.en: How was your trip?

dialogue.t: أولاً وصلنا إلى المطار متأخرين. ثمّ انتظرنا ثلاث ساعات.
dialogue.r: awwalan waṣalnā ilā al-maṭār mutaʾakhkhirīn. thumma intaẓarnā thalāth sāʿāt.
dialogue.en: First we arrived at the airport late. Then we waited three hours.
And after that?

dialogue.t: وبعد ذلك أُلغيت الرحلة، وأخيراً سافرنا في اليوم التالي.
dialogue.r: wa-baʿda dhālika ulghiyat al-riḥla, wa-akhīran sāfarnā fī al-yawm al-tālī.
dialogue.en: After that the flight was cancelled, and finally we travelled the next day.

lessons.title: Scene and event: كان… وفجأةً
lessons.learn: كان opens a scene, بينما holds a background action, and فجأةً punctuates it. كان الوقت متأخراً وفجأةً سمعنا صوتاً — the scene sits inside كان, the event steps out of فجأة.

grammar.title: Scene then event
grammar.pattern: kāna + scene · baynamā + ongoing action · wa-fajʾatan + perfect verb
grammar.explain: كان الوقت متأخراً، وكانت السماء تمطر، بينما كنّا ننتظر، وفجأةً جاءت سيارة أجرة. The scene can hold two كان clauses; the event is one perfect verb.

examples.t: كان الطريق مزدحماً وفجأةً توقف كل شيء.
examples.r: kāna al-ṭarīq muzdaḥiman wa-fajʾatan tawaqqafa kull shayʾ.
examples.en: The road was crowded and suddenly everything stopped.
While we were talking, the phone rang.
The weather was beautiful that evening.

mistakes.right: كان الطريق مزدحماً، وفجأةً توقف كل شيء.
mistakes.why: فجأة needs an event after it, and كان's predicate takes the accusative.
بينما wants an ongoing action, usually with كان.

dialogue.en: What happened at the party?

dialogue.t: كان الجميع يرقص، وفجأةً انقطعت الكهرباء.
dialogue.r: kāna al-jamīʿ yarquṣ, wa-fajʾatan inqaṭaʿat al-kahrabāʾ.
dialogue.en: Everyone was dancing, and suddenly the electricity cut out.
What did you do?

dialogue.t: بينما كنّا نبحث عن الشموع، عادت الكهرباء، وصفّق الجميع.
dialogue.r: baynamā kunnā nabḥath ʿan al-shumūʿ, ʿādat al-kahrabāʾ, wa-ṣaffaqa al-jamīʿ.
dialogue.en: While we were looking for candles, the power came back and everyone clapped.

lessons.title: The end: في النهاية، تبيّن أنّ
lessons.learn: An Arabic anecdote closes with a verdict: في النهاية، تبيّن أنّ، والحمد لله، وما زلت أذكر. It is the same move as an English punchline, with more gratitude.

grammar.title: Closing moves
grammar.pattern: fī al-nihāya… · tabayyana anna… · wa-l-ḥamdu li-llāh · taʿallamtu anna…
grammar.explain: في النهاية تبيّن أنّ التأخير كان نعمة. والحمد لله، وصلنا بسلام. The close is also how a story becomes advice — the listener gets a moral without being lectured.

examples.t: في النهاية، تبيّن أنّه كان محقاً.
examples.r: fī al-nihāya, tabayyana annahu kāna muḥiqqan.
examples.en: In the end it turned out he was right.
I learned that patience matters.

examples.t: والحمد لله، كل شيء انتهى بخير.
examples.r: wa-l-ḥamdu li-llāh, kull shayʾ intahā bi-khayr.
examples.en: Praise God, everything ended well.

mistakes.why: أنّ takes a pronoun suffix, not a bare كان.
The end of a story is one move; three of them read as filler.

dialogue.en: And how did it end with the shop?

dialogue.t: في النهاية، تبيّن أنّ الخطأ كان في الفاتورة فقط.
dialogue.r: fī al-nihāya, tabayyana anna al-khaṭaʾ kāna fī al-fātūra faqaṭ.
dialogue.en: In the end it turned out the mistake was only in the invoice.
Then you saved time and money.

dialogue.t: وتعلّمتُ أنّ الفحص قبل الدفع ضروري، والحمد لله.
dialogue.r: wa-taʿallamtu anna al-faḥṣ qabla al-dafʿ ḍarūrī, wa-l-ḥamdu li-llāh.
dialogue.en: And I learned that checking before paying is essential — praise God.

lessons.title: Inviting: هل تحبّ أن…؟
lessons.learn: Three invitation frames cover almost everything: هل تحبّ أن…؟ (would you like to), ما رأيك أن…؟ (what do you think of), and ندعوك (we invite you). Each is softer than an imperative, and each takes أن + a verb.

grammar.title: Invitation frames
grammar.pattern: hal tuḥibb an + subjunctive · mā raʾyuk an + subjunctive · nadʿūk ilā / ʿalā + noun
grammar.explain: هل تحبّ أن تتعشّى معنا؟ ما رأيك أن نزور المتحف؟ ندعوك على العشاء بمناسبة نجاحك.

examples.en: Would you like to come tomorrow?

examples.t: ما رأيك أن نتقابل بعد العمل؟
examples.r: mā raʾyuk an nataqābal baʿda al-ʿamal?
examples.en: What do you think of meeting after work?

examples.t: ندعوك على العشاء بمناسبة عيد ميلادك.
examples.r: nadʿūk ʿalā al-ʿashāʾ bi-munāsabat ʿīd mīlādik.
examples.en: We invite you to dinner for your birthday.

mistakes.why: The invitation frame needs أن before the verb.
The invitation to a meal takes على.

dialogue.t: ما رأيك أن نتقابل على العشاء الجمعة؟
dialogue.r: mā raʾyuk an nataqābal ʿalā al-ʿashāʾ al-jumʿa?
dialogue.en: What do you think of meeting for dinner on Friday?

dialogue.t: فكرة جميلة، الليلة عندي هدية أيضاً.
dialogue.r: fikra jamīla, al-layla ʿindī hadiyya aydan.
dialogue.en: Lovely idea — I also have a gift tonight.
Would you like me to invite my brother?
With pleasure — dinner grows with company.

lessons.title: Accepting and declining
lessons.learn: Yes is بكل سرور or يسعدني ذلك. No is للأسف، لا أستطيع — with a reason and an alternative. معذرة is 'excuse me', not 'no'.

grammar.title: Accept / decline + keep the door open
grammar.pattern: bi-kull surūr · li-l-asaf, lā astaṭīʿ + reason · in shāʾa Allāh, al-marra al-qādima
grammar.explain: بكل سرور، متى؟ / للأسف لا أستطيع، عندي سفر — لكن أعدك بالمرة القادمة. The last clause is not padding; it is how the relationship is kept.

examples.en: With pleasure, that would please me.
Unfortunately I cannot this time.

examples.t: أعدك أن آتي في المرة القادمة.
examples.r: aʿiduk an ātiya fī al-marra al-qādima.
examples.en: I promise to come next time.

mistakes.why: A four-word refusal with no reason closes the door.
Negation comes before the verb: لا أستطيع.

dialogue.t: هل تحبّ أن تأتي إلى الشاطئ غداً؟
dialogue.r: hal tuḥibb an taʾtiya ilā al-shāṭiʾ ghadan?
dialogue.en: Would you like to come to the beach tomorrow?
With pleasure! At what time?
Ten in the morning, and we'll stay until sunset.

dialogue.t: يسعدني ذلك، لكن للأسف عندي درس — أعدك بالمرة القادمة.
dialogue.r: yusʿidunī dhālika, lākin li-l-asaf ʿindī dars — aʿiduk bi-l-marra al-qādima.
dialogue.en: That would please me, but unfortunately I have a class — I promise next time.

lessons.title: On the phone: من المتحدث؟
lessons.learn: Phone Arabic has its own openers: الو، من المتحدث؟، لحظة من فضلك، سيصل الاتصال، الخطّ ضعيف. Digital messages keep the same politeness in writing.

grammar.title: Phone frames
grammar.pattern: alū? · man al-mutakallim? · laḥẓa min faḍlik · sa-uʿāwid al-ittiṣāl
grammar.explain: الو؟ أهلاً، من المتحدث؟ لحظة من فضلك، سأناديه. If the line breaks: الخطّ ضعيف، سأعاود الاتصال — the polite way to hang up first.

examples.en: Hello? Who is speaking?
One moment please, I'll call my brother.
The line is weak — I'll call again.

mistakes.why: من المتحدث is a fixed phrase; adding أنت breaks the frame.
The verb is عاود (to repeat), not وصل.

dialogue.en: Hello? Who is speaking?

dialogue.t: أنا زينب، هل يمكن أن أكلم سعيداً؟
dialogue.r: anā Zaynab, hal yumkin an ukallim Saʿīdan?
dialogue.en: It's Zaynab — may I speak to Saeed?

dialogue.t: أنا سعيد، لحظة من فضلك، الخطّ ضعيف قليلاً.
dialogue.r: anā Saʿīd, laḥẓa min faḍlik, al-khaṭṭ ḍaʿīf qalīlan.
dialogue.en: This is Saeed — one moment please, the line is a little weak.
Then I'll call again shortly.

items.q: «في النهاية جلسنا ساعة» — what does the teller think of friendship?
كان يحمل هدية لابنه بينما كنت أبحث عن كتاب. What is the contrast?
items.answer: a gift and a book, two errands

items.q: نحن نتقابل في الساعة التاسعة. When do they meet?

culture.text: Arabic conversation rewards the listener. A reaction like ما شاء الله or الله يعطيك العافية is expected at the right moment, and a story is judged by how the teller closes it — usually with a lesson and a thanks. Silence between turns is shorter than in English conversation: the reply, not the pause, is what holds the floor.

reading.text: قابلتُ صديقي القديم في السوق أمس. أولاً، لم أعرفه لأنّه تغيّر كثيراً. ثمّ سمعتُ صوته، وقفزتُ من مكاني. كان يحمل هدية لابنه، بينما كنت أبحث عن كتاب. وفجأةً قال: «كيف حالك يا رجل؟» في النهاية جلسنا ساعة، وتعلّمتُ أنّ الصداقة لا تحتاج موعداً.
reading.gloss: I met my old friend in the market yesterday. At first I did not recognise him because he had changed a lot. Then I heard his voice and jumped from my place. He was carrying a gift for his son while I was looking for a book. Suddenly he said, 'How are you, man?' In the end we sat for an hour, and I learned that friendship needs no appointment.

listening.script:
أ: الو؟ من المتحدث؟
ب: أنا طارق. هل تحبّ أن تتعشّى معنا الليلة؟
أ: بكل سرور! لكن للأسف عندي موعد حتى الثامنة.
ب: لا مشكلة، نتقابل في الساعة التاسعة.
listening.gloss: A: Hello, who is speaking? B: It's Tariq. Would you like to have dinner with us tonight? A: With pleasure! But unfortunately I have an appointment until eight. B: No problem — we'll meet at nine.

idioms.meaning: words that promise more than they can keep
let it go; trust it will work out

mistakes.why: The invitation frame needs أن + subjunctive.
Fixed phone phrase, without أنت.

mistakes.wrong: كان يحمل، بينما كنت أبحث، ثمّ فجأة، وفي النهاية…
mistakes.why: Arabic storytelling uses one marker at a time; a chain of markers is a list, not a story.

task.title: Tell me a two-minute story
task.instructions: Record yourself telling a real story in Arabic for two minutes: أولاً for the scene, كان for the background, فجأةً for the turn, and one closing move (في النهاية تبيّن أنّ…). Then listen back and count the reactions you left out — every 'حقاً؟' your listener needed is a place your story ran without them.
